records.source: שְׁמַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַתָּ֨ה עֹבֵ֤ר הַיּוֹם֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָבֹא֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת גּוֹיִ֔ם גְּדֹלִ֥ים וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑ךָּ עָרִ֛ים גְּדֹלֹ֥ת וּבְצֻרֹ֖ת בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Hear, Israel: you [are] crossing today the Jordan to go in to dispossess nations great and mighty more than you, cities great and fortified in the heavens,
pieces: Hear, Israel: today you are about to cross the Jordan, to go in and drive out nations greater and stronger than you, with great cities fortified up to the sky,

L.1: Hear, Israel: you [are] crossing over the Jordan today, to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified up to the heavens,

R.1: Listen, people of Israel! Soon you will cross the Jordan River. You will go in and drive out nations that are bigger and stronger than you are. Their cities are large, and their walls seem to reach the sky.

decisions.choice: you are crossing today: the crossing is close at hand
decisions.reason: The participle with "today" describes what is about to happen. Moses speaks on the plains of Moab (1:5), and the crossing comes after his death (Joshua 3). "Today" marks the moment of decision, as it often does in Deuteronomy (4:39-40; 11:26).

decisions.choice: dispossess: drive out the nations and take their place
decisions.reason: With nations as its object, the verb means to drive out a people and take over what was theirs; with the land as its object it means to take possession (verses 4-6).

decisions.choice: fortified up to the heavens: walls so high they seemed to touch the sky
decisions.reason: This is a picture of size, not a measurement. The spies used the same words (1:28), and Moses repeats them to show how impossible the conquest looked from Israel's side.

decisions.choice: Listen, people of Israel ... River ... their walls seem to reach the sky
decisions.reason: Readable says "listen" and "people of Israel", adds "River", and says that the picture is of the city walls. Literal and Balanced keep "Hear, Israel", the call that opens 5:1 and 6:4.

records.heading: Not because you are righteous

records.source: עַֽם־גָּד֥וֹל וָרָ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י עֲנָקִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ מִ֣י יִתְיַצֵּ֔ב לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י עֲנָֽק׃
records.gloss: a people great and tall, sons of Anakim, whom you, you know, and you, you have heard: who will stand before [the] sons of Anak?
pieces: a people strong and tall, the Anakim. You know about them, and you have heard it said, 'Who can stand up to the descendants of Anak?'

L.2: a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom you yourself know, and you yourself have heard [it said], 'Who can stand before the sons of Anak?'

R.2: The people there are strong and tall. They are the Anakim, a people known for their great size. You know about them. You have heard people say, 'No one can stand against the descendants of Anak!'

decisions.choice: the Anakim: a people known for their great height
decisions.reason: The spies saw them at Hebron and felt like grasshoppers beside them (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33). Moses has already named them (1:28; 2:10-11, 21), and Joshua later drives them out of the hill country (Joshua 11:21-22).

decisions.choice: who can stand before the sons of Anak?: a saying that expects the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: Moses quotes it as something Israel has heard said. Verse 3 answers it: the LORD himself crosses ahead of Israel.

decisions.choice: you yourself know, you yourself have heard: Israel knows this firsthand
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out twice with the verbs, which Hebrew does only for emphasis. Moses does not play down the danger.

decisions.choice: sons (Literal) / descendants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of" is the Hebrew way of naming the members of a people or clan. Balanced and Readable say "descendants", as Numbers 13:22, 28 do. Readable says the saying as a statement and adds who the Anakim were.

records.source: וְיָדַעְתָּ֣ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ הֽוּא־הָעֹבֵ֤ר לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵ֣שׁ אֹֽכְלָ֔ה ה֧וּא יַשְׁמִידֵ֛ם וְה֥וּא יַכְנִיעֵ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְהֽוֹרַשְׁתָּ֤ם וְהַֽאַבַדְתָּם֙מַהֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And you will know today that Yahweh your God, he [is] the [one] crossing before you [as] a fire consuming; he will destroy them and he will subdue them before you, and you will dispossess them and destroy them quickly, as spoke Yahweh to you.
pieces: So understand today that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the one who goes across ahead of you like a consuming fire. He will destroy them and bring them down before you, and you will drive them out and wipe them out quickly, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised you.

L.3: And you shall know today that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one crossing over before you [as] a consuming fire; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will subdue them before you, and you will dispossess them and destroy them quickly, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to you.

R.3: But today you can be sure of this: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will go across ahead of you. He is like a fire that burns everything up. He will destroy those nations and defeat them in front of you. Then you will drive them out and quickly wipe them out, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised you.

decisions.choice: a consuming fire: God's holy power that destroys what stands against him
decisions.reason: Moses used the same picture in 4:24, there as a warning to Israel. Here the fire goes ahead of Israel against its enemies, and the question of verse 2, "Who can stand?", is answered.

decisions.choice: he will destroy, he will subdue; you will dispossess, you will destroy
decisions.reason: The emphatic "he ... he" puts God's work first. Israel's part follows from his victory and does not replace it.

decisions.choice: quickly: each enemy falls swiftly once God goes ahead
alternatives: the whole land will be taken at once
decisions.reason: In 7:22 Moses said the nations would be cleared "little by little", not all at once. The two fit together: the nations that resist fall quickly in battle (Joshua 10-11), while the land as a whole is settled over time. "Quickly" here answers Israel's fear of the Anakim.

decisions.choice: promised
decisions.reason: The verb is "spoke". Balanced and Readable say "promised", because what the LORD spoke here was a promise (1:8; 7:1-2). Literal keeps "has spoken".

records.source: אַל־תֹּאמַ֣ר בִּלְבָבְךָ֗ בַּהֲדֹ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֹתָ֥ם׀מִלְּפָנֶיךָ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּצִדְקָתִי֙ הֱבִיאַ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה לָרֶ֖שֶׁת אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את וּבְרִשְׁעַת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֔לֶּה יְהוָ֖ה מוֹרִישָׁ֥ם מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Do not say in your heart, when drives out Yahweh your God them from before you, saying, in my righteousness has brought me Yahweh to possess the land this; and in [the] wickedness of the nations these Yahweh [is] dispossessing them from before you.
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has pushed them out of your way, do not tell yourself, 'It is because I am righteous that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought me in to take possession of this land.' No, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is driving them out before you.

L.4: Do not say in your heart, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God thrusts them out from before you, 'Because of my righteousness {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought me in to take possession of this land,' and [yet] because of the wickedness of these nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] dispossessing them from before you.

R.4: After {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has pushed these nations out of your way, do not think, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brought me into this land because I have done what is right.' No! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is driving these nations out because they are so wicked.

decisions.choice: say in your heart: think to yourself
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and decides. Moses warns against a private thought, as in 7:17 and 8:17.

decisions.choice: my righteousness: being in the right before God, a claim to have earned the land
decisions.reason: Here the word names a claim to merit: the thought that Israel received the land because it deserved it. Verses 5-6 deny it, and verses 7-24 show the opposite.

decisions.choice: and because of the wickedness of these nations: Moses' answer, not part of what Israel might say
alternatives: Israel's thought goes on: 'and because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD is driving them out'
decisions.reason: The clause has no "saying" of its own and could be read as the end of Israel's thought. But verse 5 repeats it as Moses' own statement, set against Israel's claim, so it is read here as his correction. The nations' guilt had long been building (Genesis 15:16; Leviticus 18:24-25).

decisions.choice: because I have done what is right
decisions.reason: Readable says what "righteousness" means here, a claim to have done right, in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep "righteousness" and "righteous". Verses 5 and 6 follow this.

records.source: לֹ֣א בְצִדְקָתְךָ֗ וּבְיֹ֨שֶׁר֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אַתָּ֥ה בָ֖א לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֶת־אַרְצָ֑ם כִּ֞י בְּרִשְׁעַ֣ת׀הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ מוֹרִישָׁ֣ם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ וּלְמַ֜עַן הָקִ֣ים אֶת־הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לַאֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: Not in your righteousness and in [the] uprightness of your heart [are] you going in to possess their land, for in [the] wickedness of the nations these Yahweh your God [is] dispossessing them from before you, and in order to establish the word which swore Yahweh to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
pieces: It is not because you are righteous or because your heart is upright that you are going in to take possession of their land. It is because of the wickedness of these nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is driving them out before you, and to keep the promise that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made on oath to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

L.5: Not because of your righteousness or because of the uprightness of your heart [are] you going in to take possession of their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] dispossessing them from before you, and in order to establish the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

R.5: You are not going in to take their land because you have done what is right or because your heart is honest. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is driving these nations out because they are wicked. He is also keeping the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

decisions.choice: uprightness of heart: honest, straight intentions
decisions.reason: The phrase pairs inner honesty with "righteousness". Israel can claim neither as the reason for the gift.

decisions.choice: to establish the word he swore: the land is given to keep God's oath to the patriarchs
decisions.reason: God promised the land to Abraham and confirmed it to Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 12:7; 15:18; 26:3; 28:13; Deuteronomy 1:8). The two reasons stand side by side: the nations' guilt and God's own faithfulness, not Israel's goodness.

decisions.choice: ancestors; the promise made on oath
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", and "promise" for the "word" God swore. Readable follows verse 4 for "righteousness".

records.source: וְיָדַעְתָּ֗ כִּ֠י לֹ֤א בְצִדְקָֽתְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֠לֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵ֨ן לְךָ֜ אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֖רֶף אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: And you will know that not in your righteousness Yahweh your God [is] giving to you the land good this to possess it, for a people stiff of neck [are] you.
pieces: Understand, then, that it is not because you are righteous that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people.

L.6: And you shall know that [it is] not because of your righteousness [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] giving you this good land to take possession of it, for you [are] a people stiff of neck.

R.6: So understand this: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is not giving you this good land because you have done what is right. In fact, you are a very stubborn people.

decisions.choice: stiff of neck: stubborn, refusing to be led
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox or donkey that stiffens its neck against the yoke or the reins. God used it of Israel at the golden calf (Exodus 32:9; 33:3, 5; 34:9), the event Moses now recalls (verse 13).

decisions.choice: for: the reason merit is ruled out
decisions.reason: Moses does not only deny that Israel earned the land; he gives evidence against it, which verses 7-24 set out.

decisions.choice: stiff of neck / stiff-necked / very stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, Balanced the English form of the same picture, and Readable its meaning.

records.source: זְכֹר֙ אַל־תִּשְׁכַּ֔ח אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־הִקְצַ֛פְתָּ אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר לְמִן־הַיּ֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יָצָ֣אתָ׀מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם עַד־בֹּֽאֲכֶם֙ עַד־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה מַמְרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם עִם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Remember, do not forget how you provoked to anger Yahweh your God in the wilderness; from the day that you came out from [the] land of Egypt until your coming to the place this, rebellious you have been with Yahweh.
pieces: Remember this and never forget it: how you made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God angry in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you arrived here, you have kept on rebelling against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.7: Remember, do not forget, how you provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to wrath in the wilderness. From the day that you came out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: Never forget how you made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God angry in the desert. You have been rebelling against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the day you left Egypt until you came here.

decisions.choice: remember, do not forget: one command said twice for force
decisions.reason: The positive and the negative together make the command emphatic, as in 8:2, 11, 18-19.

decisions.choice: provoked to wrath: stirred up God's anger by what they did
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in verses 8 and 22 and binds Moses' list of Israel's failures together.

decisions.choice: rebellious you have been: a lasting pattern, not one act
decisions.reason: The participle with "you have been" describes a constant way of acting. The same words close the list in verse 24, framing it (1:26, 43).

decisions.choice: kept on rebelling / have been rebelling
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a verb that shows the ongoing sense of the Hebrew participle.

records.source: וּבְחֹרֵ֥ב הִקְצַפְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְאַנַּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה בָּכֶ֖ם לְהַשְׁמִ֥יד אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And at Horeb you provoked to anger Yahweh, and was angry Yahweh with you to destroy you.
pieces: Even at Horeb you provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was so angry with you that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was ready to destroy you.

L.8: And at Horeb you provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to wrath, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with you, to destroy you.

R.8: Even at Mount Horeb you made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry enough to destroy you.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain where God made his covenant with Israel
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy calls Mount Sinai "Horeb" (1:6; 4:10; 5:2).

decisions.choice: at Horeb: placed first for emphasis, even there
decisions.reason: Moses moves from the whole journey (verse 7) to its worst moment. At the very place where the covenant was made, Israel broke it.

decisions.choice: to destroy you: anger that intended to destroy
decisions.reason: The infinitive says what the anger was set to do. God said so himself (verse 14; Exodus 32:10).

decisions.choice: Even ... so angry ... that he was ready / Mount
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "even" for the emphasis of the Hebrew word order and spell out the purpose of the anger. Readable adds "Mount" so the reader knows Horeb is a mountain.

records.source: בַּעֲלֹתִ֣י הָהָ֗רָה לָקַ֜חַת לוּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲבָנִים֙ לוּחֹ֣ת הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁר־כָּרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וָאֵשֵׁ֣ב בָּהָ֗ר אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֥א שָׁתִֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: When I went up the mountain to receive [the] tablets of the stone, [the] tablets of the covenant which made Yahweh with you, and I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights; bread not I ate, and water not I drank.
pieces: When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights without eating food or drinking water.

L.9: When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made with you, I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread, and I did not drink water.

R.9: I went up the mountain to get the stone tablets. The covenant that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made with you was written on them. I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. During that time I did not eat any food or drink any water.

decisions.choice: the tablets of the covenant: the stone tablets with the Ten Words, the covenant's written terms
decisions.reason: The tablets held the commandments God spoke at Horeb (4:13; 5:22; Exodus 24:12; 31:18). They were the written record of the covenant.

decisions.choice: bread: food of any kind
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general. With "water" it describes a complete fast.

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights
decisions.reason: Exodus 24:18 gives the length of the first stay on the mountain, and Exodus 34:28 records the fast of the second. Moses fasts the same length again in verse 18.

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "food", the sense of "bread" here. Literal keeps "bread".

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶת־שְׁנֵי֙ לוּחֹ֣ת הָֽאֲבָנִ֔ים כְּתֻבִ֖ים בְּאֶצְבַּ֣ע אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַעֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כְּֽכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר֩ יְהוָ֨ה עִמָּכֶ֥ם בָּהָ֛ר מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵ֖שׁ בְּי֥וֹם הַקָּהָֽל׃
records.gloss: And gave Yahweh to me two [the] tablets of the stone written by [the] finger of God, and on them according to all the words which spoke Yahweh with you on the mountain from [the] midst of the fire on [the] day of the assembly.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me the two stone tablets written by the finger of God. On them were all the words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day of the assembly.

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me the two tablets of stone, written by the finger of God, and on them [were written] all the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me the two stone tablets. God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} had written on them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own finger. They held all the words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you from the fire on the mountain, on the day all the people gathered there.

decisions.choice: written by the finger of God: written by God himself, not by a human hand
decisions.reason: The same words are used in Exodus 31:18 and 32:16. The magicians of Egypt used the phrase of God's power at work (Exodus 8:15).

decisions.choice: according to all the words: the tablets held exactly what God had spoken
decisions.reason: God wrote down what Israel had heard him say aloud, and added nothing more (5:22).

decisions.choice: the day of the assembly: the day Israel gathered at Horeb to hear God
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy uses the phrase for that day (10:4; 18:16; compare 4:10).

decisions.choice: God himself ... with his own finger; the day all the people gathered there
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's finger and the meaning of "the day of the assembly".

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶת־שְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָאֲבָנִ֖ים לֻח֥וֹת הַבְּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of forty days and forty nights, gave Yahweh to me two [the] tablets of the stone, tablets of the covenant.
pieces: At the end of the forty days and forty nights, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

L.11: And it came about at the end of forty days and forty nights [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

R.11: At the end of those forty days and nights, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me the two stone tablets with the covenant written on them.

decisions.choice: at the end of forty days: the account of verses 9-10 is picked up again
decisions.reason: Moses repeats the giving of the tablets to set it beside what follows: at the very moment God gave the covenant, the people below were breaking it (verse 12).

decisions.choice: with the covenant written on them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the tablets of the covenant" as in verse 9.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י ק֣וּם רֵ֤ד מַהֵר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹצֵ֖אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם מַסֵּכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, arise, go down quickly from here, for has acted corruptly your people which you brought out from Egypt; they have turned quickly from the way which I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Get up and go down from here at once, because your people whom you brought out of Egypt have become corrupt. They have been quick to turn from the way I commanded them; they have made themselves an idol of cast metal.'

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have acted corruptly. They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image.'

R.12: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Get up and hurry down from here. Your people that you brought out of Egypt have done something very evil. They have quickly turned away from the way I told them to live. They have made a metal idol for themselves.'

decisions.choice: your people whom you brought out: God speaks of them as Moses' people
decisions.reason: God says the same in Exodus 32:7, as if disowning the people. In his prayer Moses gives the words back: they are "your people" whom "you brought out" (verses 26, 29).

decisions.choice: acted corruptly: ruined themselves by sin
decisions.reason: The verb means to spoil or ruin. Moses used it for making an idol (4:16, 25). Its other sense, "destroy", returns in Moses' plea "do not destroy your people" (verse 26).

decisions.choice: cast image: an idol made by pouring melted metal into a mold
decisions.reason: Exodus 32:4 tells how the calf was made from the people's gold earrings.

decisions.choice: the way: the way of life God commanded
decisions.reason: "Way" is the path a person walks, the whole manner of life the commandments lay out (5:33).

decisions.choice: done something very evil; the way I told them to live
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what acting corruptly was and what "the way" means here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֑ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, saying, I have seen the people this, and look, a people stiff of neck [is] it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} also said to me, 'I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, saying, 'I have seen this people, and look, it [is] a people stiff of neck.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'I have watched these people. They are very stubborn.

decisions.choice: the LORD said ... saying: a second word of God follows the first
decisions.reason: Verse 12 told Moses to go down; this speech gives God's judgment on the people. Exodus 32:9-10 has the same order.

decisions.choice: stiff of neck: stubborn
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: look / indeed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws attention to what is seen. Literal says "look"; Balanced says "indeed"; Readable leaves it to the plain statement.

records.source: הֶ֤רֶף מִמֶּ֨נִּי֙ וְאַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וְאֶמְחֶ֣ה אֶת־שְׁמָ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֽוֹתְךָ֔ לְגוֹי־עָצ֥וּם וָרָ֖ב מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Let alone from me, that I may destroy them, and I may blot out their name from under the heavens, and I will make you into a nation mighty and numerous more than it.
pieces: Leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, so that I can destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and larger than they are.'

L.14: Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under the heavens, and I will make you into a nation mightier and more numerous than they.'

R.14: Leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, so that I can destroy them and wipe out their name from the earth. Then I will make you into a nation that is stronger and bigger than they are.'

decisions.choice: let me alone: God's word leaves room for Moses to plead
decisions.reason: God tells Moses to stand aside, as in Exodus 32:10. The command assumes that Moses could hold him back. Moses does not leave him alone but falls down and prays (verses 18-20, 25-29).

decisions.choice: blot out their name from under the heavens: destroy them so that no one remembers them
decisions.reason: The same threat is spoken against Israel's enemies (7:24; 25:19). Here it falls on Israel itself.

decisions.choice: I will make you into a nation: a new beginning with Moses, as with Abraham
decisions.reason: God's promise to Abraham was "I will make you into a great nation" (Genesis 12:2). He offers Moses the same at Horeb and later at Kadesh (Exodus 32:10; Numbers 14:12).

decisions.choice: wipe out; from the earth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "wipe out" for the picture of blotting out writing. Readable says "from the earth" for "from under the heavens", meaning anywhere in the world.

records.source: וָאֵ֗פֶן וָֽאֵרֵד֙ מִן־הָהָ֔ר וְהָהָ֖ר בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּשְׁנֵי֙ לֻחֹ֣ת הַבְּרִ֔ית עַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֥י יָדָֽי׃
records.gloss: And I turned and I went down from the mountain, and the mountain [was] burning with fire, and two [the] tablets of the covenant on two my hands.
pieces: So I turned and went down from the mountain while it was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.

L.15: And I turned and went down from the mountain, and the mountain [was] burning with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant [were] in my two hands.

R.15: So I turned around and went down the mountain. The mountain was still burning with fire. I was carrying the two covenant tablets, one in each hand.

decisions.choice: the mountain burning with fire: the sign of God's presence still on it
decisions.reason: The fire on the mountain is the fire from which God spoke (4:11; 5:23; Exodus 19:18). Moses comes down from God's presence to the people's idol.

decisions.choice: in my two hands: both tablets carried by Moses
decisions.reason: The detail sets up verse 17, where he throws them from his two hands.

decisions.choice: still; one in each hand
decisions.reason: Readable adds "still" to show the fire had not gone out, and says how "my two hands" held the tablets.

records.source: וָאֵ֗רֶא וְהִנֵּ֤ה חֲטָאתֶם֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם לָכֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה סַרְתֶּ֣ם מַהֵ֔ר מִן־הַדֶּ֕רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I saw, and look, you had sinned against Yahweh your God; you had made for yourselves a calf, a cast image; you had turned quickly from the way which commanded Yahweh you.
pieces: I looked, and there it was: you had sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You had made yourselves a calf cast in metal. You had been quick to turn from the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded you.

L.16: And I looked, and look, you had sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You had made yourselves a calf, a cast image. You had turned aside quickly from the way that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded you.

R.16: When I looked, I saw that you had sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You had made a metal idol shaped like a calf. You had quickly turned away from the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded you to live.

decisions.choice: a calf: the figure of a young bull
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East the bull stood for strength and was linked with gods. The people hailed the calf as the gods who brought them out of Egypt (Exodus 32:4-6), and Jeroboam later set up calves in the same way (1 Kings 12:28).

decisions.choice: you had turned quickly from the way: what God told Moses, Moses now sees
decisions.reason: Moses repeats God's own words from verse 12. His eyes confirm what he had been told on the mountain.

decisions.choice: look / there it was
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of sudden discovery in the Hebrew word that Literal renders "look". Readable follows verse 12 for "the way".

records.source: וָאֶתְפֹּשׂ֙ בִּשְׁנֵ֣י הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וָֽאַשְׁלִכֵ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י יָדָ֑י וָאֲשַׁבְּרֵ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I took hold of two the tablets, and I threw them from on two my hands, and I broke them before your eyes.
pieces: So I seized the two tablets, threw them down from my hands, and smashed them before your eyes.

L.17: And I took hold of the two tablets and threw them from my two hands, and I broke them before your eyes.

R.17: So I took hold of the two tablets and threw them down. I broke them to pieces right in front of you.

decisions.choice: I broke them before your eyes: a public sign that the covenant had been broken
decisions.reason: The tablets were the written covenant. Moses breaks them in front of the people, who had already broken what was written on them (Exodus 32:19).

decisions.choice: took hold: seized firmly
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp or seize. Moses did not drop the tablets; he threw them down on purpose.

decisions.choice: down; to pieces
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the tablets were thrown, and Readable that they were broken to pieces.

records.source: וָֽאֶתְנַפַּל֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה כָּרִאשֹׁנָ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי עַ֤ל כָּל־חַטַּאתְכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲטָאתֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I prostrated myself before Yahweh as the first, forty days and forty nights; bread not I ate, and water not I drank, because of all your sin which you had sinned by doing the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh to provoke him.
pieces: Then I lay face down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as I had the first time, for forty days and forty nights, without eating food or drinking water, because of all the sin you had committed by doing what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.

L.18: And I prostrated myself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread, and I did not drink water, because of all your sin that you had sinned, doing what was evil in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.

R.18: Then I lay face down on the ground in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for forty days and nights, just as I had done before. I did not eat any food or drink any water. I did this because of all the sin you had committed. You had done what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is evil, and you had made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: prostrated myself: lay flat on the ground in prayer
decisions.reason: Lying face down before God was the posture of urgent pleading (verse 25; Numbers 16:22).

decisions.choice: as at the first: a second forty days, like the first stay of verse 9
alternatives: "as at the first" means "as I had first lain before the LORD", a prayer not otherwise recorded
decisions.reason: Moses compares this period with the first: again forty days and nights without food or water. Exodus 34:28 records a forty-day fast when the tablets were given again. Whether verses 18 and 25 describe that same stay or another period of prayer is not said; Moses orders his account by its point, Israel's guilt and his prayer, more than by the order of events (compare 10:10).

decisions.choice: doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD: doing what the LORD judges evil
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means in someone's judgment (4:25; 17:2).

decisions.choice: prostrated myself / lay face down; in the eyes of / in the sight of / what the LORD says is evil
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the reflexive verb; Balanced and Readable describe the posture. Balanced says "in the sight of", and Readable says plainly whose judgment it is.

records.source: כִּ֣י יָגֹ֗רְתִּי מִפְּנֵ֤י הָאַף֙ וְהַ֣חֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָצַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד אֶתְכֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י גַּ֖ם בַּפַּ֥עַם הַהִֽוא׃
records.gloss: For I was in dread from before the anger and the wrath which was angry Yahweh against you to destroy you; and listened Yahweh to me also at the time that.
pieces: I was terrified of the anger and fury {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} felt against you, enough to destroy you. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to me that time too.

L.19: For I was in dread of the anger and the wrath with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry against you, to destroy you. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to me that time also.

R.19: I was afraid because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was so angry with you that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was ready to destroy you. But once again {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to me.

decisions.choice: I was in dread: deep fear
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong word for fear (28:60). Moses feared what God's anger would do to the people.

decisions.choice: the anger and the wrath: two words together for the force of God's anger
decisions.reason: Hebrew joins near-synonyms to make the sense stronger.

decisions.choice: that time also: God had listened to Moses before
decisions.reason: The word "also" assumes earlier times when God answered Moses' prayers for the people (Exodus 15:25; 17:4-6; Numbers 11:2; 14:20).

decisions.choice: was ready to
decisions.reason: Readable puts "to destroy you" as what God was ready to do, giving the sense of the infinitive.

records.source: וּֽבְאַהֲרֹ֗ן הִתְאַנַּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה מְאֹ֖ד לְהַשְׁמִיד֑וֹ וָֽאֶתְפַּלֵּ֛ל גַּם־בְּעַ֥ד אַהֲרֹ֖ן בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽוא
records.gloss: And with Aaron was angry Yahweh very to destroy him; and I prayed also for Aaron at the time that.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, and at that time I prayed for Aaron as well.

L.20: And with Aaron {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry, to destroy him; and I prayed also for Aaron at that time.

R.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was also very angry with Aaron and was ready to destroy him. So at that time I prayed for Aaron too.

decisions.choice: Aaron: the one who made the calf
decisions.reason: Aaron gathered the gold, made the calf and built an altar before it (Exodus 32:1-6, 21-25). Exodus does not record a prayer for him; Moses adds it here. Aaron lived on to serve as priest and died at Mount Hor (10:6; Numbers 20:28).

decisions.choice: very angry, to destroy him: anger great enough to destroy him
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, the infinitive says what the anger was set to do.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the prayer was Moses' answer to God's anger with Aaron.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־חַטַּאתְכֶ֞ם אֲשֶׁר־עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אֶת־הָעֵ֗גֶל לָקַחְתִּי֮ וָאֶשְׂרֹ֣ף אֹת֣וֹ׀בָּאֵשׁ֒ וָאֶכֹּ֨ת אֹת֤וֹ טָחוֹן֙ הֵיטֵ֔ב עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־דַּ֖ק לְעָפָ֑ר וָֽאַשְׁלִךְ֙ אֶת־עֲפָר֔וֹ אֶל־הַנַּ֖חַל הַיֹּרֵ֥ד מִן־הָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And your sin which you had made, the calf, I took, and I burned it in the fire, and I crushed it, grinding well until that it was fine to dust; and I threw its dust into the wadi the [one] coming down from the mountain.
pieces: Then I took the sinful thing you had made, the calf, and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw the dust into the stream that flows down the mountain.

L.21: And your sin that you had made, the calf, I took and burned it with fire, and I crushed it, grinding [it] well, until it was as fine as dust; and I threw its dust into the stream that comes down from the mountain.

R.21: Then I took the calf, the sinful thing you had made, and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it into a fine powder. Then I threw the powder into the stream that flows down from the mountain.

decisions.choice: your sin, the calf: the calf itself is called "your sin"
decisions.reason: The idol is named by the sin it embodied: the thing in which Israel sinned.

decisions.choice: burned, crushed, ground, threw away: destroyed so that nothing remained to worship
decisions.reason: Exodus 32:20 tells the same and adds that Moses made the people drink the water. Later kings who removed idols did the same (2 Kings 23:6, 15).

decisions.choice: the stream: water running down from the mountain in a stream bed
decisions.reason: The word names a stream or the valley it runs in, often dry outside the rainy season. Here water was flowing, so the dust was carried away.

decisions.choice: your sin / the sinful thing; dust / powder
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the sinful thing" so that the calf is not read as an act. Readable says "powder" for metal ground as fine as dust.

records.source: וּבְתַבְעֵרָה֙ וּבְמַסָּ֔ה וּבְקִבְרֹ֖ת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה מַקְצִפִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And at Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah provoking to anger you were Yahweh.
pieces: At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah you also made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry.

L.22: And at Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah you were provoking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to wrath.

R.22: You also made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry at other places: at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah.

decisions.choice: Taberah, Massah, Kibroth-hattaavah: places named after Israel's rebellions
decisions.reason: Taberah ("burning") is where the LORD's fire burned among the complaining people (Numbers 11:1-3). Massah ("testing") is where they tested the LORD over water (Exodus 17:1-7; Deuteronomy 6:16). Kibroth-hattaavah ("graves of craving") is where those who craved meat were buried (Numbers 11:31-34).

decisions.choice: you were provoking: not in order of time
decisions.reason: Massah came before Horeb, the others after it. Moses gathers examples from the whole journey (verse 7) to show a constant pattern; the participle stresses that it kept happening.

decisions.choice: also ... at other places
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "also" to link these to the calf, and Readable says these are other places.

records.source: וּבִשְׁלֹ֨חַ יְהוָ֜ה אֶתְכֶ֗ם מִקָּדֵ֤שׁ בַּרְנֵ֨עַ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲלוּ֙ וּרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לָכֶ֑ם וַתַּמְר֗וּ אֶת־פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֤א הֶֽאֱמַנְתֶּם֙ ל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And when sent Yahweh you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, go up and possess the land which I have given to you, and you rebelled against [the] mouth of Yahweh your God, and not you believed him, and not you listened to his voice.
pieces: And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent you out from Kadesh-barnea and said, 'Go up and take possession of the land I have given you,' you rebelled against the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You did not trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.23: And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, 'Go up and take possession of the land that I have given you,' you rebelled against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you did not believe {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.

R.23: Then at Kadesh-barnea {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent you out and said, 'Go up and take the land I have given you.' But you rebelled against what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded. You did not trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you did not obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Kadesh-barnea: where Israel refused to enter the land
decisions.reason: Moses told the story in 1:19-46 (Numbers 13-14). The people were afraid of the Anakim (1:28), the same fear verses 1-3 answer.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the LORD: what the LORD said, his command
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the same refusal in 1:26, 43.

decisions.choice: believe: trust, rely on
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold firm to someone, to rely on what he says. Israel did not trust that God could give them the land (1:32; Numbers 14:11).

decisions.choice: listen to his voice: obey
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what he says.

decisions.choice: trust; obey; command
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "trust" for believing a person, "obey" for listening to his voice, and "command" for his mouth. Literal keeps the Hebrew pictures.

records.gloss: Rebellious you have been with Yahweh from [the] day of my knowing you.
pieces: You have been rebelling against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the day I first knew you.

L.24: Rebellious you have been against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the day that I knew you.

R.24: You have been rebelling against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} ever since I have known you.

decisions.choice: from the day I knew you
alternatives: from the day he became known to you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has Moses speak: "from the day I knew you". The ancient Greek translation reads "from the day he became known to you", which points the verse to God and to his first making himself known to Israel. Reviewers should check the evidence before this is approved.

decisions.choice: rebellious you have been: the close of the list begun in verse 7
decisions.reason: The same words opened the list in verse 7. They frame the whole account of Israel's failures.

decisions.choice: Rebellious you have been
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which puts "rebellious" first for emphasis.

records.gloss: And I prostrated myself before Yahweh the forty the days and the forty the nights which I prostrated myself, because had said Yahweh to destroy you.
pieces: So I lay face down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} those forty days and forty nights, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would destroy you.

L.25: And I prostrated myself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the forty days and the forty nights that I prostrated myself, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would destroy you.

R.25: I lay face down on the ground in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for those forty days and nights, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would destroy you.

decisions.choice: the forty days and forty nights that I prostrated myself: the same period as verse 18
decisions.reason: With the article ("the forty days") Moses points back to the time named in verse 18. After the list in verses 22-24 he returns to it to give the words of his prayer (verses 26-29). See verse 18 on how this period relates to the account in Exodus.

decisions.choice: had said to destroy you: had declared that he would destroy them
decisions.reason: "Said" with "to destroy" states God's stated intent (verses 14, 19).

decisions.choice: that he would
decisions.reason: All levels supply the words English needs for "said to destroy"; Literal brackets "that". Balanced and Readable follow verse 18 for the posture.

records.gloss: And I prayed to Yahweh, and I said, Lord Yahweh, do not destroy your people and your inheritance which you redeemed by your greatness, which you brought out from Egypt by a hand strong.
pieces: I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, '{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, do not destroy {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own inheritance, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

L.26: And I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, '{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, do not destroy {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.

R.26: I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I said, '{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, do not destroy {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. They belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You set them free by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power. You brought them out of Egypt with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty strength.

decisions.choice: your people and your inheritance: they belong to God
decisions.reason: God had called them Moses' people (verse 12); Moses gives them back to God. An inheritance is a family's own land, held for good; Israel is the LORD's own possession (4:20; 32:9).

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free at a cost, as a slave is bought out
decisions.reason: The verb is used of freeing Israel from the house of slavery (7:8; 13:6). Moses appeals to what God has already done.

decisions.choice: Lord Yahweh: the title "Lord" before the divine name, an address of humble appeal
decisions.reason: Moses used the same address when he pleaded with God in 3:24.

decisions.choice: with a strong hand: by God's power at work
decisions.reason: The hand is a picture of strength in action (4:34; 5:15; 6:21).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: When the title "Lord" stands just before the divine name, the name is printed "GOD" to avoid "Lord LORD"; the Yahweh setting gives "Lord Yahweh".

decisions.choice: They belong to you; set them free; great power
decisions.reason: Readable says what "inheritance" means here and says "set free" for "redeemed". Balanced and Readable say "great power" for "greatness".

records.source: זְכֹר֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֑ב אַל־תֵּ֗פֶן אֶל־קְשִׁי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאֶל־רִשְׁע֖וֹ וְאֶל־חַטָּאתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not turn to [the] stubbornness of the people this, and to its wickedness, and to its sin,
pieces: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their wickedness and their sin,

L.27: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not turn to the stubbornness of this people, or to its wickedness, or to its sin,

R.27: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not pay attention to how stubborn these people are, or to their wickedness and their sin.

decisions.choice: remember your servants: an appeal to God's promise to the patriarchs
decisions.reason: To ask God to remember is to ask him to act on what he promised. Moses makes the same appeal at the calf in Exodus 32:13; the promise is the oath of verse 5.

decisions.choice: servants: those who belong to a master and serve him
decisions.reason: The word names someone owned by a master, not hired. Said of God's servants it is a title of honor for those who belong to him and do his will (Genesis 26:24; Numbers 12:7).

decisions.choice: stubbornness: hardness, refusal to yield
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the root of "stiff" in "stiff of neck" (verses 6, 13).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal) / servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the hard edge of the word; Balanced and Readable say "servants", which does not bring in the picture of modern slavery.

decisions.choice: turn to / look at / pay attention to
decisions.reason: To turn to something is to give it attention. Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

records.source: פֶּן־יֹאמְר֗וּ הָאָרֶץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹצֵאתָ֣נוּ מִשָּׁם֒ מִבְּלִי֙ יְכֹ֣לֶת יְהוָ֔ה לַהֲבִיאָ֕ם אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וּמִשִּׂנְאָת֣וֹ אוֹתָ֔ם הוֹצִיאָ֖ם לַהֲמִתָ֥ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: lest say the land which you brought us out from there: from not being able Yahweh to bring them into the land which he spoke to them, and from his hatred of them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.
pieces: Otherwise the people of the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought us out of will say, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} could not bring them into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised them, and because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hated them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them out to kill them in the wilderness."

L.28: lest the land from which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought us out say, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not able to bring them into the land of which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them, and because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hated them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out to kill them in the wilderness."

R.28: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy them, the people of Egypt will say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} could not bring them into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised them. He hated them, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took them out into the desert to kill them."

decisions.choice: the land ... say: the people of that land, the Egyptians
decisions.reason: A land stands for the people who live in it. Moses makes the same appeal in Exodus 32:12 and Numbers 14:13-16.

decisions.choice: an appeal to God's name among the nations
decisions.reason: Moses argues that destroying Israel would let the nations say God was weak or cruel. His reputation is bound up with his people.

decisions.choice: brought us out: Moses counts himself with the people
decisions.reason: Moses had been offered a new nation of his own (verse 14), but he speaks as one of those God brought out.

decisions.choice: the people of the land; If you destroy them ... Egypt
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of the land". Readable names Egypt and says what "lest" refers to: what would follow if God destroyed Israel.

decisions.choice: promised
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, Balanced and Readable say "promised" for what the LORD spoke of; Literal keeps "spoke".

records.gloss: And they [are] your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your strength the great and by your arm the outstretched.
pieces: Yet they are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought out by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} outstretched arm.'

L.29: And they [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought out by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great strength and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} outstretched arm.'

R.29: But they are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. They belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You brought them out with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong arm.'

decisions.choice: outstretched arm: God's power reaching out to act
decisions.reason: The phrase pairs with "strong hand" for the power God showed in the exodus (4:34; 5:15; Exodus 6:6).

decisions.choice: and they: but they, set against the nations' charge
decisions.reason: The prayer ends where it began (verse 26): whatever the nations say, these are God's own people. The account goes on in 10:1 with the new tablets.

decisions.choice: They belong to you; strong arm
decisions.reason: As in verse 26, Readable explains "inheritance". It says "strong arm" for the picture of an arm stretched out in power.
